learning_objective: 🎯 Learn to draft crisp, clear, and formal notices to announce events, meetings, or lost & found items!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A notice must ALWAYS be enclosed in a box. The format is: Name of Institution, the word 'NOTICE', Date, Heading, Body of the Notice, and finally your Signature, Name, and Designation.
The body of the notice must answer 5 questions: What is happening? When is it happening? Where is it? Who is it for? Whom to contact? (5 Ws: What, When, Where, Who, Whom).
Keep it strictly to 50 words. Do not write unnecessary stories or greetings. Be direct and to the point.
Never use first or second person pronouns like 'I', 'me', or 'you' in general notices. Use third person and passive voice (e.g., 'All students are hereby informed...').
For lost items, give specific details (color, brand). For found items, don't give away all details—ask the owner to identify it first.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Find the Missing Detail
fun_activity.instructions: Read this line: 'A debate competition will be held next Monday in the school.' What is missing? (Hint: The 5 Ws! We don't know the exact TIME or WHO can participate. Always check the 5 Ws!)

exam_tips: 📌 NEVER forget to draw the box using a pencil. No box = marks deducted.
📌 Write the word 'NOTICE' in CAPITAL letters.
📌 Stick strictly to the 50-word limit. Examiners cut marks for exceeding it.
quick_recap: ⭐ Format: Institution -> NOTICE -> Date -> Heading -> Body -> Sign/Name/Designation.
⭐ The opening line should be: 'This is to inform all the students...'
⭐ Notices are meant for a specific target audience, not the general public.
